marisol: Quick heads-up — planning question on parental leave timing & paperwork for David's upcoming leave. @david said he'd be out around mid-August. Can we confirm what forms we need, pay/benefits coverage, and manager coverage checklist? cc @jenna

david: Hey! Partner's due ~Aug 15. Plan is to start leave ~Aug 12 and take about 12 weeks. What do I need to submit and how does pay work? Also curious about health coverage while I'm out.

jenna: Congrats, David! Short version: Redwood's policy supports paid parental leave and benefits continuity but specifics depend on primary vs secondary caregiver status. Paperwork: 1) LOA form in Workday (leave request), 2) hospital/birth confirmation or birth certificate after delivery, 3) for prenatal bedrest a physician's note. If FMLA applies we'll also need the FMLA paperwork (we'll fill that out with you). Use the internal portal: https://hr.redwood.com/leave or via Okta app `Leave Portal`. Email leaves@redwood.com if you prefer.

david: Appreciate it. I'm expecting to be secondary caregiver — what does that mean for paid weeks? Also what happens to 401(k) deferrals and medical premiums during paid leave?

jenna: As a non-primary (secondary) caregiver you're generally eligible for 6 weeks fully paid parental leave. Primary caregivers typically get 16 weeks. While you're on approved paid leave Redwood continues employer-paid health/dental/vision premiums. 401(k): payroll will continue contributions during paid payroll cycles; if any portion of your leave is unpaid, employee deferrals pause for those pay periods (you can make up contributions after return). Payroll coordinates any adjustments once leave is approved. You can also use accrued PTO to extend paid time.

marisol: Manager-side logistics — please prepare a brief handoff doc (1-pager) and list of on-call contacts. People Ops can help source interim coverage if needed. Managers: remember to set an OOO on calendars and update routing for key tickets.

david: Question — do I need the docs before the leave starts or can I submit after? Partner might be on bedrest beforehand.

jenna: If it's pre-birth bedrest, submit LOA with the physician's note (that's necessary to approve leave starting earlier). For normal start date you can submit the LOA with expected dates in advance and upload the birth confirmation after. We usually ask for LOA at least 30 days ahead when possible.

jenna: I'll open an internal case for tracking: case-2024-0423. Next steps for you: 1) file LOA in Workday, 2) attach any docs you have (doctor note if applicable), 3) confirm official start date with your manager. We'll loop payroll and benefits.

mira (hr-bot): Leave request created: #35842 for david. Steps: submit LOA form, attach docs, manager approval required. Payroll will process pay schedule once LOA approved. Estimated processing time: 3-5 business days.

david: Thanks — last quick thing: does Redwood provide any childcare support (stipend, backup care) or flexible return programs? Also what's the return-to-work ramp policy?

jenna: Yes — we offer a childcare stipend for the first 6 months after return (amount varies by region, typical US amount: $100/month) and backup care vouchers you can request via People Ops. We also have a flexible return program (reduced hours option) for up to 8 weeks post-return; managers work with People Ops to set it up. All details are in the benefits page and we'll add them to your case.

marisol: Perfect — I'll drop a short checklist for managers in the channel (handoff template, coverage steps, communication bullets). @david we'll DM for any private details and get everything started. :tada:
